item.title: Scale your AI workloads faster and more efficiently with GKE Pod snapshots (4 minute read)
item.description: Google Kubernetes Engine adds Pod snapshots, capturing a workload's running CPU and GPU memory state to restore it on demand, cutting AI inference startup by up to 89 percent and loading a 70B parameter model in 37 seconds. Codeway's Retake cut startup to eight seconds using the feature.

item.title: Better prompt caching for GPT-6 (3 minute read)
item.description: OpenAI launched an improved prompt caching system for the GPT-6 family that delivers higher cache hit rates by default. Developers get discounts of up to 90% on cached input tokens when the system reuses shared prefixes within a 30-minute window. New tools include a Prompt Caching Dashboard to track hit rates and a diagnostics tool to investigate unexpected misses. Developers can also prewarm the cache to reduce latency or adjust reasoning effort between responses without breaking cache.

item.title: Cloudflare Introduces the Agent Development Stack Lifecycle to Replace Traditional SDLC (2 minute read)
item.description: Cloudflare introduced an Agent Development Lifecycle to replace traditional software pipelines with autonomous, event-driven systems for AI coding agents, built on its Workflows product and a new @cloudflare/ci tool. It adds OpenTelemetry-based observability and an Agent Access Model that issues short-lived, capability-limited credentials to prevent lateral movement.

item.title: Teaching a 9B model to investigate production alerts (9 minute read)
item.description: Datadog fine-tuned Qwen3.5-9B on traces from a larger teacher model to automate change attribution during incident investigations. The specialized student model achieved 87% of the teacher's recall while reducing inference costs by roughly 20 times to $0.003 per investigation. A single 40 GB A100 GPU can support approximately 100,000 of these investigations per week.

item.title: AI Now: Tech Workers Inquiry (6 minute read)
item.description: AI systems increasingly depend on hidden layers of human labor, including data labeling, content moderation, model evaluation, and other forms of contract work that shape how models behave. Making those labor relationships visible helps explain where AI systems get their capabilities, how failures are caught, and which costs are shifted onto workers outside the companies building the models.

item.title: Peak traffic shouldn't mean peak anxiety (Sponsor)
item.description: Traffic skyrocketing? If you're on Microsoft Azure, there's no reason to panic. When user demand spikes, Azure adjusts capacity in the background. Performance stays steady with no manual intervention, no late-night firefighting, and no scrambling to explain why the site went down during the big launch. Build without limits with Azure

item.title: Model Optimizer (GitHub Repo)
item.description: NVIDIA has open sourced its Model Optimizer library, which offers techniques like quantization, pruning, and distillation to accelerate deep learning models. The tool supports inputs from Hugging Face, PyTorch, or ONNX and exports optimized checkpoints for deployment frameworks like TensorRT-LLM and vLLM. Users can install the stable release via PyPI or use NVIDIA container images with the software pre-installed.

item.title: Harness-sdk (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Strands Agents is a new open-source SDK for building AI agents in Python and TypeScript. It offers a "harness" with benchmarked defaults for models and memory, or developers can use the underlying SDK to write their own agent loops. The toolkit includes support for tools, structured output, and model providers such as Amazon Bedrock, Anthropic, and OpenAI.

item.title: Docker Sandbox Kit Spec: Authority as Code (7 minute read)
item.description: The Docker Sandbox Kit Specification v3 defines how to package an agent's permissions and dependencies as an ordinary OCI image. The format specifies network rules, credentials, and volumes, allowing developer tooling to scan, sign, and diff agent authority changes. Docker Sandboxes is the first conforming runtime for the open source specification.

item.title: Global AI routing with <1% overhead on multi-cluster GKE Inference Gateway (6 minute read)
item.description: Google's multi-cluster GKE Inference Gateway pools globally distributed accelerator capacity behind a single endpoint, routing LLM traffic based on live KV-cache utilization rather than round-robin. A 17,000-node benchmark across three regions showed near-linear throughput scaling with less than 1 percent routing overhead and a 99.9 percent success rate.

item.title: Observability and Application Performance Monitoring (APM) for AWS (Sponsor)
item.description: When an alert fires on Amazon ECS, a tutorial in AWS Marketplace walks you through the trace to root cause, one path instead of five dashboards. Read the tutorial.

item.description: Amazon CloudWatch Omni is a unified observability experience for application and AI workloads.

item.title: Advancing Private AI Compute with secure, server-side memory (3 minute read)
item.description: Google is adding a persistent, encrypted memory layer to its Private AI Compute platform, letting AI assistants retain context across devices while keeping data unlockable only with device-held keys.

item.title: ClusterMAX 3.0: The Industry Standard GPU Cloud Rating System Returns (163 minute read)
item.description: SemiAnalysis's ClusterMAX 3.0 report rates 77 GPU cloud providers out of 323 tracked, drawing on over 200 customer interviews and testing across audit, performance, and reliability phases.

item.title: Prometheus and OpenTelemetry interoperability in 2026 - Survey results (5 minute read)
item.description: A survey of 81 active OpenTelemetry users found that the average rating for ease of use with Prometheus rose to 3.6 in 2026, up from 3.1 in 2024. No respondents this year described the interoperability as "very difficult." Nearly half of participants use a hybrid approach for infrastructure metrics, mixing Prometheus and OpenTelemetry instrumentation styles.

item.title: Kubernetes v1.37: Tracking When a PersistentVolumeClaim Was Last Used (Beta) (3 minute read)
item.description: Kubernetes v1.37 promotes the PersistentVolumeClaimUnusedSinceTime feature gate to Beta, enabling it by default. The PVC protection controller adds an Unused condition to each PersistentVolumeClaim to indicate whether a running pod references it. This eliminates the need for custom tooling to identify orphaned storage. Administrators can use the condition's timestamp to find PVCs that have been idle for specific periods.

item.title: Python Workers are now generally available (8 minute read)
item.description: Python Workers are now generally available on the Cloudflare Developer Platform. The runtime natively supports Cloudflare bindings, so developers can connect to services like R2 and D1 without writing JavaScript code. Users can also run frameworks like FastAPI, Django, and Flask or integrate AI libraries like langchain and openai.

item.title: Markdown in /src (6 minute read)
item.description: Markdown can serve as the durable source of intent for agent-generated software, capturing architectural, data, API, and implementation decisions that would otherwise disappear in ephemeral prompt sessions. Keeping that Markdown alongside code in /src makes it diffable, reviewable, and available to both humans and agents, while tests can be derived from it to verify the resulting implementation.

item.title: What Sun got wrong (6 minute read)
item.description: Sun Microsystems paired strong technology and strategy with weak operational execution, including basic failures in sales and customer responsiveness. A 2005 startup running OpenSolaris tried to buy Sun hardware but struggled to get a response, while Dell quickly handled pricing, financing, and delivery—an example of how neglecting the mechanics of running the business can erase technical advantages.

item.title: Cutting CI pipeline time by 64%: What actually works in production (6 minute read)
item.description: An engineering team reduced their Merge Train pipeline duration from one hour to 22 minutes, a 64% reduction. They achieved this while growing their test suite by 90% and improving CI health from 82% to above 90%. Infrastructure costs rose roughly 10%, but the team estimates they regained over 1,300 engineer hours previously lost to delays and retries. Key changes included upgrading to Intel hardware and separating service tests from browser-based tests.

item.title: Your infrastructure has enough moving parts. Your VPN shouldn't add more routes, rules, and exceptions to manage. (Sponsor)
item.description: Tailscale replaces the patchwork with a single encrypted mesh: every resource gets its own identity and connects directly, no site-to-site tunnels, no overlapping subnets, no hairpinning. New clusters join with rules in place. Try Tailscale free.[Try Tailscale free]

item.title: Treg (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Treg provides a unified API proxy for over 3,000 endpoints across 60+ providers, covering categories like SEO, social media, and company enrichment. The service allows agents to make calls starting at one cent using a shared pool of provider accounts. Users can avoid monthly subscriptions for tools like Semrush or Moz by paying per call, or they can connect their own keys for unmetered access.

item.title: Ax (GitHub Repo)
item.description: AX is a high-throughput, declarative orchestrator designed to run billions of autonomous agent workloads in a Kubernetes cluster. The tool provides primitives to isolate agents, fence their networks, and prevent runaway costs. It is currently under active development, with warnings that major breaking changes will likely occur before a stable release.

item.title: Google Named a Leader in the External Threat Intelligence Service Forrester Wave (5 minute read)
item.description: Forrester named Google a Leader in its External Threat Intelligence Service Providers Wave for Q3 2026, citing perfect scores across nine criteria and autonomous Gemini-powered agents for triage, detection engineering, and threat hunting that customers say surface 139 percent more threats.

item.title: Microsoft Open-Sources TauGrid to Simplify AI Workload Management on Kubernetes (2 minute read)
item.description: Microsoft has open-sourced TauGrid, a Kubernetes platform that unifies scheduling, queuing, and monitoring for GPU-based AI training and inference through a single Helm install, built on Kueue and KubeRay, with planned support for multi-tenant workspaces and DeepSpeed and LoRA workflows.

item.title: AI is accelerating code. Who's governing the database changes? (Sponsor)
item.description: Liquibase Secure 6.0 brings human and AI-driven database change under the same governance, with centralized policy, visibility, and control built into existing delivery workflows. See it in action →

item.description: Tanner Linsley released TanStack Charts, a framework-agnostic, grammar-of-graphics charting library for TypeScript built largely with AI coding agents, working across React, Vue, Svelte, and other frameworks while remaining in Alpha with a smaller bundle size than Chart.js or Observable Plot.

item.title: AI Has No Wisdom and Neither Will You (5 minute read)
item.description: LLMs can generate working code without developing the long-term judgment needed to keep systems maintainable, because qualities like good architecture and evolvability often reveal themselves only months or years later.

item.title: OpenAI Introduces Triage Framework and Case Studies to Report Model Misalignment (2 minute read)
item.description: OpenAI introduced a formal process for tracking, investigating, and publicly disclosing model misalignment across training and deployment, releasing six initial case studies showing models fabricating data, hiding mistakes in compaction summaries, and bypassing resource restrictions during testing.

item.title: AWS Elastic Beanstalk introduces Cluster Mode (4 minute read)
item.description: AWS Elastic Beanstalk now offers a fully managed Cluster Mode that runs applications on infrastructure powered by Amazon EKS. The feature allows teams to operate multiple applications that share resources, lowering per-application costs without adding operational complexity. AWS does not charge extra for Cluster Mode, but users pay for the underlying resources, including the EKS control plane and compute.

item.title: New Low-Cost Burstable Amazon EC2 T8i Instances Are Generally Available (3 minute read)
item.description: AWS launched general availability of burstable EC2 T8i instances on custom Intel Granite Rapids processors, offering up to 30 percent better price performance than T3, higher compute and network bandwidth, and free tier eligibility for the micro and small sizes.

item.title: When Scanners Miss the Attack: How Cloudflare Client-Side Security Protects Storefronts (21 minute read)
item.description: Cloudflare's Page Shield ML system uncovered four malicious JavaScript campaigns hijacking affiliate commissions, cloaking ad fraud, and running a remote code execution backdoor on e-commerce sites, detecting all eight payloads even though most were missed by VirusTotal and URLScan.

item.title: Grit your teeth and ship it (5 minute read)
item.description: Strong builders can become reluctant shippers because they notice every flaw and want systems to feel elegant and complete before release. In large codebases, progress often requires accepting imperfect but consistent solutions, and producing a steady volume of work tends to outperform polishing a small number of projects indefinitely because quality and audience response are hard to predict.

item.title: Enforce agent controls in the harness, not the gateway (Sponsor)
item.description: Gateways only secure what you route through them, sandboxes stop reach, not actions, and SIEM shows risk too late. Ory Agent Security is the first identity and access control plane that enforces inside the agent harness. Now usable via simple plugin. Give your agents identities of their own. See how

item.title: security-audit (GitHub Repo)
item.description: A new coding-agent skill turns an AI agent into a security auditor that orchestrates reconnaissance, vulnerability hunting, and validation. The tool runs a structured audit in six phases and classifies findings into three verdicts: confirmed, needs_validation, or rejected. Audits against the same repository are additive, using prior results to target gaps or revalidate changed source code. The skill activates automatically when an agent receives a request for a security audit or pen-test.

item.title: Higgsfield (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Higgsfield is an open-source GPU orchestration and machine learning framework designed for training models with billions to trillions of parameters. The framework aims to simplify distributed training by managing environments and reducing the need for complex configuration files. It supports standard PyTorch workflows and has been tested on AWS and Lambda Labs.

item.title: RADAR: Catch gray failures with anomaly detection (4 minute read)
item.description: Gray failures allow specific service components to fail silently while health checks remain green, often leaking revenue for hours before detection. Databricks built a system called RADAR to catch these partial outages by identifying sudden spikes in user errors. The system reduced incident discovery time by 95% with over 90% precision. Users can build a similar detection pipeline on the Databricks platform using a template available on GitHub.

item.title: Saving another 100TB of RAM with math (and Rust) (11 minute read)
item.description: Cloudflare reduced the memory footprint of its Pingora Backend Router by 100TB through algorithmic optimizations to the pingora-ketama library. The team determined they could remove 90% of the hashes generated for each server without causing errors or collisions. They rolled out the change in stages to avoid invalidating cached content across the network all at once.

item.title: Kubernetes v1.37: Pod-Level Resource Managers graduated to Beta (2 minute read)
item.description: The Pod-Level Resource Managers feature has graduated to Beta status in Kubernetes v1.37. This enhancement allows the Kubelet to use pod-level resource declarations when making hardware placement decisions. It solves a previous limitation where operators had to choose between dedicating physical cores to sidecars or forfeiting NUMA alignment.

item.title: Salesforce staggers back to feet after global outage (4 minute read)
item.description: Salesforce experienced an hours-long global outage affecting hundreds of instances, causing severe delays, intermittent errors, and inaccessible services, due to requests stalling on an internal login service and exhausting server resources. A validated fix was deployed fleetwide, but some instances required manual restarts and continued experiencing scheduled-job failures.

item.title: How to automate Docker Registry creation with Harness Pipelines and Terraform (14 minute read)
item.description: Harness demonstrates a three-stage CI/CD pipeline that uses Terraform to dynamically provision a unique Docker virtual registry and Docker Hub upstream proxy, builds and pushes an image, then deploys it to Kubernetes with rolling updates and automatic rollback. Output variables and Harness expressions connect resources across stages without hardcoding.

item.title: I don't like LLMs (4 minute read)
item.description: LLMs can be highly useful while still being unpleasant to interact with because they present fabricated and correct information with the same confident, human-like tone. AI agents also reflect the values and culture of the companies that build them, making trust, behavior, and interaction design important alongside raw model capability.

item.title: Running OpenBao on Kubernetes with a CloudNativePG PostgreSQL backend (9 minute read)
item.description: OpenBao and CloudNativePG can manage infrastructure secrets on Kubernetes without vendor lock-in by using certificate authentication and synchronous replication. OpenBao uses the CloudNativePG PostgreSQL cluster as an encrypted key-value store, and a schema-init job revokes default public permissions to lock down the database. CloudNativePG automatically renews client certificates every 90 days, but OpenBao requires a rolling restart to load the new files. The setup runs three OpenBao replicas and three Postgres instances across separate nodes.

item.title: Browserskill (GitHub Repo)
item.description: BrowserSkill connects AI agents such as Cursor, Claude Code, and Codex to a user's logged-in browser. The tool requires agents to explicitly borrow open tabs and return them after finishing a task. It includes a command-line interface, a daemon, and a browser extension.

item.title: Cline (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Cline is an open-source coding agent that runs in IDEs, terminals, and as a native desktop app for macOS and Windows. It reads project structures, edits files, and executes terminal commands with human-in-the-loop approval. Users can switch between Plan and Act modes or use the SDK to build custom tools and coordinate multi-agent teams. The tool runs on any model and supports integrations through plugins or MCP servers.

item.title: Komodor Extends AI SRE Reach for Kubernetes to AI Agents (3 minute read)
item.description: Komodor launched an Agentic Operations Platform that lets SREs deploy, customize, govern, and audit AI agents through familiar DevOps workflows, with 50+ built-in agents, integrations, guardrails, approvals, and spending controls. The platform aims to help teams manage growing fleets of production AI agents while preserving existing change management and governance practices.

item.title: Getting started with runtime security and Falco (11 minute read)
item.description: Runtime security protects cloud workloads while they are executing, filling gaps that posture management cannot catch, such as zero-days, privilege escalation, and compromised credentials. Falco provides cloud-native runtime detection across hosts, containers, Kubernetes, and cloud services by analyzing system calls and plugin events, adding contextual alerts, and deploying easily with Helm.

item.title: HarnessTax: How Much Does the Harness Matter for Coding Agents? (8 minute read)
item.description: Coding-agent harnesses such as Claude Code, Codex CLI, and Pi can produce similar task success rates while using dramatically different amounts of tokens and money. Across 21 model–harness combinations on SWE-bench Lite and Terminal-Bench 2.0, harness choice changed cost by as much as 5×, and the model provider's own harness was not consistently the most efficient option.

item.title: Have it both ways: stay discoverable in search while disallowing AI training (8 minute read)
item.description: Cloudflare has launched a new Disallow AI Training setting that allows website owners to block AI training while remaining indexed for search. Apple, Google, and Microsoft have committed to honoring this preference, which resolves the tradeoff created by mixed-use crawlers. Cloudflare plans to introduce more granular controls for AI summaries by early next year.

item.title: Cilium 1.20: Gateway API ExternalAuth, TCPRoute/UDPRoute, ENI IPAM for IPv6, and more (19 minute read)
item.description: Cilium 1.20 adds IPv6 support for AWS ENI IPAM and introduces datapath plugins to let third parties extend the eBPF datapath without forking the project. The release also promotes the Multi-Cluster Services API to a stable status and deprecates the legacy mutual authentication feature in favor of the ztunnel proxy. Other updates include a per-pod option to disable source IP verification and a new ClusterNetworkPolicy for admin-level guardrails.

item.title: Kubernetes v1.37: Memory QoS Graduates to Beta (3 minute read)
item.description: Memory QoS has graduated to Beta in Kubernetes v1.37 and is now enabled by default. The feature uses the memory controller on Linux nodes running cgroup v2 to guide the kernel on container memory treatment. The default memoryThrottlingFactor changed to null in this release, ensuring that upgrading clusters does not automatically throttle existing workloads.

item.title: Internal Developer Portals: Why Native CI/CD Drives Scale (7 minute read)
item.description: Native CI/CD integration transforms internal developer portals from documentation and service catalogs into scalable workflow platforms, enabling developers to create, deploy, and roll back services without manually configuring pipelines. It also lets platform teams centrally enforce golden paths, promotion policies, and governance while reducing pipeline drift and operational complexity.

item.title: How runtime insights helps with container security (4 minute read)
item.description: Runtime insights provide continuous visibility into live container behavior, enabling real-time threat detection, risk prioritization, faster incident response, and continuous compliance. Using technologies such as eBPF, runtime context also helps AI agents understand infrastructure and deliver more actionable security triage and remediation while reducing noise from traditional static scanning.

item.title: Open Code Review (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Open Code Review is an open source AI-powered code review CLI tool that originated as Alibaba Group's internal official assistant. It has served tens of thousands of developers and identified millions of code defects. The tool uses a hybrid architecture that combines deterministic engineering with an LLM agent to generate structured review comments with line-level precision.

item.title: Openresearch (GitHub Repo)
item.description: OpenResearch is a local-first workspace that turns coding agents like Claude Code and Cursor into research agents. The platform can autonomously propose ideas, change code, launch experiments, and analyze evidence. Users can run workspaces locally, over SSH, or on platforms including Kubernetes and Hugging Face Jobs.

item.title: Let's not water down the terms Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery (5 minute read)
item.description: Continuous Integration means merging all changes into a shared mainline at least daily, while Continuous Delivery means keeping software deployable at all times through automated pipelines. The author argues both terms are precise and well-documented, not vague, and warns against diluting their meaning as happened with Agile and DevOps.

item.title: Infrastructure identity for platform engineers (10 minute read)
item.description: Infrastructure identity replaces static credentials and fragmented access controls with short-lived, cryptographically verified identities for humans, workloads, machines, and AI agents. Platform teams can embed just-in-time, policy-driven access into developer workflows, reducing security risk and operational toil while improving access times, auditability, and control over increasingly autonomous infrastructure.

item.title: Coding is hard. Coding securely should be easy. (Sponsor)
item.description: 1Password streamlines developer secrets management, and makes sure that AI agents never see or store raw credentials.

item.description: On-demand state repartitioning is available in Public Preview on Databricks Runtime 18 and above.

item.description: New Relic Lens is now generally available, allowing users to query external data sources like Snowflake and Google Sheets within the New Relic UI.

item.description: AI-assisted development is making software creation dramatically faster, but production readiness lags as agents favor simple infrastructure over security, scalability, observability, and operational resilience.
